Executive Overview

Summary of AXP's long-term stock trajectory and key investor takeaways
From an adjusted closing price of $1.22 on June 01, 1972 to $305.99 on March 11, 2026, AXP delivered a cumulative total return of 24,894.87%, equating to a compounded annual growth rate of 10.81% over 53.8 years. The worst peak-to-trough drawdown was -83.91% (peak July 19, 2007 at $49.30 → trough March 06, 2009 at $7.93). Over the full period, $34.27 per share was returned to shareholders via dividends.

Key takeaways for investors:

  • AXP has demonstrated strong long-term capital appreciation, with its adjusted price growing from under $1.25 to over $300.
  • Despite multiple severe drawdowns — notably the 2008 Global Financial Crisis — the stock has historically recovered and continued its upward trajectory.
  • Consistent dividend payments underscore AXP's commitment to returning capital to shareholders, with dividends accelerating in recent decades.
  • The stock's annualized volatility of 34.69% reflects meaningful price risk, particularly during financial-sector stress events.

AXP, as a financial services company with significant credit-card exposure, was among the hardest-hit Dow components during this period. The COVID-19 crash of 2020 also produced a sharp but comparatively shorter drawdown, with the stock recovering to new highs within months rather than years.
